advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile `create_defaults` parsing with its documented 'free-form' contract (either allow non-string values or update docs/docstrings to say create_defaults values must be strings).
evidence: mapping_config.py:177 `axes = { name: _parse_axis_map(raw[name], where=f"{where}.{name}") for name in _AXIS_MAPS if name in raw }` — `_AXIS_MAPS` includes `create_defaults`
mapping_config.py:130 `elif isinstance(val, str):` … else raises `MappingConfigError` — only str/SKIP allowed
docstring line 323 `create_defaults`` is ungated`` and docs/config.md `[mapping.default.create_defaults]  # ungated create-time field defaults (free-form)`
validate() docstring: "``create_defaults`` is ungated" — yet the parse layer type-gates it to strings
advisory.finding: `create_defaults` is documented as "free-form" / "ungated create-time field defaults" but is parsed by `_parse_axis_map`, which rejects any non-string value. A `create_defaults` entry with an int, list, or nested table (e.g. `priority = 3` or a labels list) fails closed at load, contradicting the documented free-form contract.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether unknown keys inside a mapping layer table should fail closed (or at least warn), and add a parse-time check + test if so.
evidence: mapping_config.py:177-181 iterates only `for name in _AXIS_MAPS if name in raw`
mapping_config.py:183-190 reads only the four named vocab keys and `hierarchy`; no branch rejects/reports leftover keys in `raw`
module docstring/commit claim: "fail-closed" parsing — but unknown intra-layer keys are neither warned nor errored
ABSENCE: no test in test_mapping_config.py covers an unknown key within a layer table
advisory.finding: `_parse_layer` silently ignores unknown keys inside a layer table (only keys in `_AXIS_MAPS`, the four vocab names, and `hierarchy` are consumed). In a module that advertises fail-closed parsing, a typo such as `staus_map` or `statues` is silently dropped rather than rejected, so the intended mapping is silently absent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm SKIP-sentinel coercion is intended for `create_defaults` (which is otherwise free-form/ungated); if not, exclude create_defaults from SKIP handling.
evidence: mapping_config.py:128 `if val == SKIP:` applied uniformly to all five axis maps including `create_defaults`
docs/config.md: create_defaults example `labels = "rebar"` implies arbitrary literal string values are intended
advisory.finding: Any axis-map value equal to the string `"skip"` is coerced to the SKIP sentinel via `val == SKIP`, including under `create_defaults`. A user cannot express a literal `"skip"` create-default value, and the coercion is silent.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_core_is_provider_neutral with a behavioral neutrality check (assert no adapters.jira module imported after loading mapping_config).
evidence: present = [lit for lit in jira_value_literals if lit in source]
The neutrality contract (no adapter import) is behaviorally verifiable by importing the module and inspecting sys.modules / attempting resolution, rather than grepping the implementation text.
advisory.finding: test_core_is_provider_neutral asserts on the TEXT of the source file under test (reads mapping_config.py and greps for 'adapters.jira' and Jira value literals) rather than observable behavior. This is source-grepping of source code under test: it breaks on behavior-preserving edits (e.g. renaming the synthetic placeholder tokens, adding a comment mentioning a literal) with no behavior change, and passes even if a real import were performed via an alias the grep misses.
scenarios: A future refactor renames placeholder tokens or restructures docstrings, breaking the grep without any behavior change.
An adapter import introduced via an aliased/dynamic import evades the literal-substring grep and the test still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import mapping_config in isolation and assert that no 'adapters.jira*' module appears in sys.modules attributable to it, instead of substring-grepping the source file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add validate() cases for has_link_types=False/has_priorities=False/has_hierarchy=False gates and for type_map/link_map values outside their declared vocabularies.
evidence: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/mapping_config.py:330-341 gates type_map, link_map, priority_map, and hierarchy separately, plus lines 343-345 check status_map/type_map/link_map vocab.
Test only covers: '(b) capability-absent axis reference: a type_map on a target with no types' (line 183-187) and status_map-outside-vocab (line 176-181).

No test constructs Capability(has_link_types=False)/has_priorities=False with a non-empty link_map/priority_map, nor Capability(has_hierarchy=False) with a declared hierarchy, nor a type_map/link_map value outside issue_types/link_types.
advisory.finding: validate()'s capability-gate branches for link_map (has_link_types), priority_map (has_priorities), and declared hierarchy (has_hierarchy) are never exercised by a test; only has_types is. Likewise _check_vocab for type_map (issue_types) and link_map (link_types) is untested — only status_map vocab is checked. A regression that dropped or mis-wired any of these gates/checks would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor that swaps the has_link_types and has_priorities arguments, or drops the hierarchy gate, passes all tests.
A regression that only checks status_map against its vocab and skips type_map/link_map vocab is not detected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend test_validate_fails_closed with parametrized cases exercising each capability gate (link, priority, hierarchy) and each vocab check (issue_types, link_types).
